spans.s:
Śayāṇḍaka is the form in the taittirīya Saṃhitā of the name of an animal which in the Maitrāyaṇī and Vājasaneyi Saṃhitās is written as śayaṇḍaka. Some sort of bird is meant according to Roth, but the commentator on the taittirīya Saṃhitā equates the word with kṛkalāsa, ‘chameleon.’
Foot notes v. 5, 14, 1.
iii. 14. 14.
xxiv. 33.
St. Petersburg Dictionary, s.v. Cf. Zimmer, Altindisches Leben, 95.

Śayana in the Atharvaveda and later denotes a ‘couch.’ Cf. talpa, vahya.
Foot notes iii. 25. 1; v. 29. 8.
Śatapatha brāhmaṇa, xi. 5, 1, 2; 7, 4.

Śayu is the name in the Rigveda of a protégé of the Aśvins, who made his cow to give milk.
Foot notes i. 112, 16; 116, 22; 117, 20; 118, 8; 119, 6; vi. 62, 7; vii. 68, 8; x. 39, 13; 40, 8.

Śāyasthi is the name of a teacher in the vaṃśa brāhmaṇa.
Foot notes Indische

Sāya denotes ‘evening’ in the Rigveda and later, usually appearing in the adverbial form Sāyam, ‘in the evening.’ Cf. Ahar.
Foot notes taittirīya brāhmaṇa, i. 5, 3, 3; kauṣītaki brāhmaṇa, ii. 8; Śatapatha brāhmaṇa, vii. 3, 2, 18.
Rv. v. 77, 2; x. 146, 4; Av. iii. 12, 3; iv. 11, 12; viii. 6, 10, etc. Cf. Sāyaṃprātar, ‘morning and evening,’ Av. iii. 30, 7; xix. 39, 2, etc.
1. Sāyaka denotes ‘arrow’ in the Rigveda (ii. 33, 10; iii. 53, 23; x. 48, 4).
2. Sāyaka jāna-śruteya (‘descendant of Janaśruta’) kāṇḍviya is the name of a teacher, a pupil of janaśruta kāṇḍviya, in the Jaiminīya upaniṣad brāhmaṇa (iii. 40, 2).

Sāyakāyana (‘descendant of sāyaka’) is the patronymic of Śyāparṇa in the Śatapatha brāhmaṇa, and also of a teacher, a pupil of kauśikāyani in the second vaṃśa (list of teachers) in the Bṛhadāraṇyaka upaniṣad.
Foot notes x. 3, 6, 10; 5, 2, 1.
iv. 5, 27 (Mādhyaṃdina = iv. 6, 3 kāṇva).

सायकायन

Sāyakāyana, 1, 155, sobhari, 1, 261, saukarāyaṇa, 1, 155, should be read for sāyakāyana, sobhari, and saukarāyaṇa respectively.
Several misprints are due to the loss of diacritical marks: thus for Ajya read ājya, 2, 20; for Arcatka, Ārcatka, 2, 357; for Artava, ārtava, 1, 63; for Apayā, āpayā, 1, 218; for Amikṣā, āmikṣā, 1, 250; for Aśuṃga, āśuṃga, 2, 387; for Asandī, āsandī, 2, 383; for Dirghatamas, dīrghatamas, 1, 366; for Satapatha, Śatapatha, 1, 18, 34, 55, 67, 111, 119, 157, 242, 291, 371, 463, 516, 523; 2, 24, 80, 220, 221, 358, 362, 433; for Srauta, śrauta, 1, 18, 55, 281, 282, 373; 2, 34, 71, 281, 301; for Sāṅkhāyana, śāṅkhāyana, 1, 257, 281, 400, 469; 2, 34, 87, 281, 383; for Sāṭyāyanaka, Śātyāyanaka, i. 407; for sāvasāyana, Śāvasāyana, 2, 376.
